evidence.appropriate: the keystone completes the ring: the loop holds once the last piece is in; one sentence; plain (Everyman) and enclosing (Caregiver); carried only at sizes where the joints show
evidence.distinctive: a ring is the commonest logo shape; with one separated segment it reads like a progress ring or a donut chart, a cousin of the fintech list's pie
evidence.simple: a ring and one stone, 16 anchors; drawable in one stroke and two cuts
evidence.legible: holds at 16 px as a closed ring (round 2's favicon closes the joints); the segment reads from 48 px; wordmark x-height 9.7 px at 120 px
evidence.adaptable: one colour and reversed hold, and the icon is the ring; but the natural motion for a ring with a segment is a spin, which is a loading spinner
evidence.timeless: no avoid-list trend; concentric rings and apertures are the AI-era cliche only when the brand is AI, which Keystone is not
evidence.universal: at 48 to 64 px a ring with a separated top segment reads as a loading spinner or progress ring (the University of California 'loading icon' case); round 1's open favicon read as a power symbol, which round 2 closed
evidence.clear: description searches ('circle ring logo with one separated segment') found many segmented-ring and pie stock marks (Vecteezy 26452111, Dreamstime, Shutterstock 'circle segment logo'); nothing specific to the name
evidence.congruent: symmetric, heavy, low complexity and framed (a ring encloses) match; shape 0.4 misses (fully round) and dynamism 0.2 misses (a ring implies rotation)
evidence.system: horizontal, stacked, symbol, compact, small and favicon all build; the favicon is a closed ring; rationale draft in critique.md
